I can't tell from the where the previous areas of supply and demand are, but after a large swing down I'm presuming we might be at an area of HTF demand. If that's the case...and I wanted to take a QM "IN THE HTF", then I'd be looking preferably for a bullish QM . I've marked the purple bullish QM at the bottom of the swing. YES, the price doesn't return to a low enough area to buy from. BUT, price goes on to engulf the high u mark as QM (and more significantly the HH too). If u had taken the bearish QM setup as u indicate, then I think there's some lovely PA here to at least let u out of the trade with minimal damage limitation and maybe even flip the trade for profit. The engulf of HH is a warning. It may well take your stops if they are pretty tight, but if not then there's a good chance of a return to the source of the engulf (green box). The price shot up strongly from here, so there's a good chance of buy orders still sitting ( it's also an indication that's as low a buying point as the purple bullish QM watchers are going to get). It would be wise to exit the bearish QM trade here and might also be a good scalp long. I guess the price structure u labelled turned out to be more of a diamond, but regardless of what price pattern we call it, it's the IT's job to shake us out of positions and I think in this instance they did their jobs pretty well. I think it's important to keep in mind that these patterns do fail from time to time. the IT's HAVE to make them fail otherwise it would be all too easy to read their intentions, but I think what I'm learning from RTM is the fact that although these patterns do fail from time to time, there is quite a clue develops about it's failure which allows us to get out with minimal damage...or https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=775 7/38 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 32 - RTM Community indeed reverse our trade. Risk free account application: www.the5ers.com QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU The Quasimodo #799 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=775 34/38 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 32 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT astro Offline Trader Posts: 346 Thank you received: 287 Great idea Benhur. Here goes for me ... Please refer to the QM article, and lets gather a list of price events that qualifies a valid Quasimodo: 1. A swing high forms at a S/R zone - Big Money places their 1st round of Sell Orders here. Novices join in the selling. 2. Price creates a swing low - Big Money starts buying here 3. A new Swing High forms - Big money pushes price thru the previous swing high to a new supply level, taking out stops to help fill their sell orders. 4. Price drops rapidly creating a lower low - big money sell orders are filled and price drops rapidly taking out previous demand. Stops are triggered causing prices to rise. 5. Price creates a new swing high in the zone of the 1st swing high. QM level. Big money piles on more sell orders which allows price to drop from here and confuses traders.. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Larry Levin QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU The Quasimodo #492 Andyfx Offline Trader Posts: 72 Thank you received: 107 Great work DT, nothing to say How do you manage entry and stop loss at QM left shoulder level and Head Cap? Usually I perfer Entry at Head level, because stop loss is well defined, many times I miss trade at left shoulder level because not enough RR if stop loss is beyond head level. Some basic options are: - if head and shoulder levels are not too far entry at shoulder with stop beyond head - if they are a bit far half position at shoulder and half at head, both SL beyond head level - if they are far: entry at shoulder with tight stop loss beyond shoulder level DP, and if price comes to head taking that little stop loss and re-enter at head level. What do you think? Aware traders see the oncoming HTF supply, the ITs know this, so just before the HTF supply they turn price creating a nice area to be faked for later on, confusing a lot of traders who were long and using the HTF supply as their targets, this would cause a lot of traders to panic and exit their longs early and cause a drop in price assisting the ITs with their intentions, which is to create a low which can be faked later on. 2. The ITs have joined in selling with the retail, this would entice traders who were aware of the HTF supply to go short now, thinking that price has turned before the supply creating panic and fear of missing the move AKA: trigger-happy sellers. The ITs know this, and know there are millions of buy stops to be had, to assist them in reaching HTF supply. 3. This is where it gets fun! Notice the high above (Marked with a line), there will no doubt be a lot of sellers there attempting to fade the high with their stops just above, this gives the ITs and incentive to smash this level and take the LQ for the push up in to supply, this attracts BO buyers, and on this account they would have been ok, if they were not greedy, however not the brightest move buying into supply, but they would have been ok in this case for a little while, and are currently enjoying the free ride up. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=525 30/42 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 22 - RTM Community Putting them aside for one moment; we are now in HTF supply, and who waits at HTF HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT supply??? Sellers and lots of them. The ITs know this and where are we taught to put our stops?? Just outside of the zone, the ITs know this, and in this case they engulf the zone collecting all of those buy stops to sell into. But hold on, engulfed the zone, should price not go higher??? Yes it should, if it was an engulf, more than likely there was a supply just above this zone that the ITs used to FO into, a clever move created by the ITs on unsuspecting traders. 4. With all the buy stops for the ITs to sell into, they have enough LQ to drop this baby!! And this is exactly what they do. This will create panic for the BO buyers from earlier and encourage them to sell adding fuel to the move, also this will attract sellers that were short at supply originally to short again, what do we call this?? Oh yes, CHASING PRICE, NOT A RECOMMENDED PRACTICE. We have now arrived at an S/R flip area, and as most of us know, these areas attract traders attempting to fade the area even though we've just come out of supply, BO sellers in the anticipation price will break the support level. What price does in this instance is collect more LQ, faking up and down, collecting more LQ from all these small FOs for the push down, this forms a nice supply zone, lining neatly with our QM level. Think about this for a moment, these levels attract BO sellers, and also traders who are attempting to fade, with all these short up and down moves (price Faking out) this would have triggered in most of the BO sellers and stopped them out collecting their buy stops, also doing the same for the traders trying to fade the level, triggering them in and stopping them out. A nice way to get short would you not agree? 5. The ITs have pushed price down, and pushed it hard, this again will attract more BO selling, but don't forget the LTF traders getting stopped out who are going long at minor demand zones, this all adds to the ITs LQ. We now have reached the low (2) Do we see a break of this level and a continuation or do we see a FO, we wait for the ITs to make their move. They FO the area this stops a load of traders who were fading the low again giving sell stops for the ITs to buy into, and this would be our Lower low of the QM formation. With all this LQ and remembering the BO sellers will begin panicking once they see price reverse and will begin thinking of closing their position i.e. buying. This will cause confusion among traders, and encourage revenge trade after revenge trade taking loss after loss, filling the accounts of the big cats as they're smiling all the way to the bank. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=525 31/42 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 22 - RTM Community 6. Larry Levin QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU The Quasimodo Set Up Simple #574 projectsagana Offline Trader When you want to SUCCEED as much as much as you want to BREATHE, then you will be successful Posts: 579 Thank you received: 826 This is how I understand QMs They appear at the end of a bullish or bearish trends, so it's a reversal trade set up. Price action needs these things to happen for Bearish QMs: 1. Pre-existing up trend with HLs + HHs 2. Price makes HH into HTF Supply 3. Price makes a bearish engulf or a newly formed RBD/DBD inside HTF Supply 4. Price drops breaking most recent demand, support, or previous low. Makes LL https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=550 26/30 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 23 - RTM Community 5. Price then rallies up to the origin of the bearish engulf or the newly formed RBD/DBD HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT inside the HTF Supply 6. Price is then expected to significantly drop into a new downtrend. Money Here's for the Bullish QMs: 1. Pre-existing down trend with LHs + LLs 2. Price makes LL into HTF Demand 3. Price makes a bullish engulf or a newly formed DBR/RBR inside HTF Demand 4. Price rallies breaking most recent supply, resistance, or previous high. Makes HH 5. Price then drops down to the origin of the bullish engulf or the newly formed DBR/RBR inside the HTF Demand 6. Price is then expected to significantly rally into a new uptrend. Now, I can spot the QM formation on chart, But I am not sure I understand what it actually tells me in terms of PA and Price Dynamics. I would like to ask you to publish some link references of where I can dive into this stuff. Thank you Gil QM is a reversal pattern if used in the right locations. The best place (as always) to really assess it's potential is to look at your charts. You'll learn more by looking at your charts than you will any book or forum - get the basics from here and then go and spend hours pouring over your charts until spotting QM's etc and where / how to trade them are part of your subconscious. In terms of the 'why' they work, let's take a short QM setup... 1. When it forms the 2nd high this is where the professional money is shorting - this is also where novice sellers / weak hands have placed there stops and breakout / trend traders have placed long orders. 2. Price making the 2nd low is in affect the tip off that a reversal is coming - a seasoned trader spots this and is looking to short. If this new low also happens to trigger a break https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=50 30/37 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 3 - RTM Community of a significant level / TL then all the better - the more noticeable the location the more HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT likely clever traders are looking to enter the market with shorts. Of course the new low also trips some stops and encourages novice shorts on board who look to bail out as price retraces - breakout traders are weak players who don't hold for long - this helps the 'distribution' process and allows the Pro's to load up shorts on the retrace to form the RS - you should be able to predict where this RS 'should' form. 3. The process is complete - Pro traders are fully loaded on shorts, weak hands have been had their orders utilised for liquidity and now the reversal can play out. No access to charts right now but look over a chart and think about who is participating and why at each 'leg' and what their orders are doing to price and it should become clear...have a go at annotating a chart and I'll review over the weekend when I get some time. Posts: 463 Thank you received: 910 FXformula, I'm afraid those are not QMs from my point of view. Take another look at the QM article, and read this thread. Also, before going to find more QMs, maybe consider what they are. They are an effort by somebody to take the weaker players out of the market, so they can more easily move price in the direction they choose. A QM is used to fake out people in both directions. So, the extreme of the QM should look like it faked something, ideally. Attachments: 11/33 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=75 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 4 - RTM Community QUICKHROEPMLYE REPELYDUCQAUTOITOEN FORUM MORE LOGOUT THANK YOU Binyamin's Quasimodo Homework #86 bcho018 Offline Trader Posts: 114 Thank you received: 93 Hi all! Initially I had a difficult time understanding Quasimodo, but after listening to the video 3 times and going through your homeworks I think I understand better now. Quasimodo as I am lead to believe is a ritual performed at important levels by the big boys to maximize their profits from the retail traders. Step 1: Look for a return to the supply or demand Step 2: When the price return to that S/D level go to the lower timeframe Step 3: For supply, look for a high, a low then a higher high, a lower low and then a high ideally at the last high level. Vice versa for demand. And viola that is your quasimodo. This is a reverse Diamond formation, which is a Bullish Pattern, The price wanted to complete the diamond formation, so it went up touched the flag Limit (C) taking out all the pending sell orders there, then came down sharply breaking the demand (1) to attract novice seller's or Breakout seller's and from diamond demand flag Limit (Swap) (2), it went up sharply, changing the trend to up. So what you thought was a Quasimodo is actually a trap laid down by the institutions. And hence your target was not achieved and price hit your stop loss. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=1125 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 46 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT The Quasimodo #1131 corsica Away Associate Trader Posts: 335 Thank you received: 567 Hello everyone. This is the first time I post some charts. I would like to thank IF and all other for the fantastic education available here. Three months ago I was still plotting MAs and macds . Yesterday I was trying to make sense from my boxes, zones etc when suddenly I realised that I had a beautiful QM happening just in front of my nose. It was the first time I saw one live. It's terrifying. I initially took screenshots of the differents stages of the move but It was too messy so I will put only the first one and then the whole move in cleaner charts. What I took from this : For a QM to be valid you want: -an EG of a FL/ftr from a pole into consolidation. -a FO of the consolidation ( which is in fact the filling of the HTF SD) -a second engulf of your FL back into the pole as confirmation. -Then you wait at QM level. -If you miss it or are not filled you have a second chance because the price will pull back at the level of the initial FL. I understand the reference to the hunchback Quasimodo from the book but personally I would have named it Hannibal the Cannibal... Or Jack the Ripper I am not sure of all this so help and comments are welcome ! Have a great week end. Most SD traders still look directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading. It's further left again we should be looking. Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely simple stuff. We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves. one more from Pedini: www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum...tups? start=325#22279 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=1200 16/38 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 49 - RTM Community AttachHmOenMtsE: EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT The following user(s) said Thank You: moogroo, ViTaLDRuG, Frosty, nsikandar PA PA PA PA Plan Ahead our Personal Approach to the Price Action in both Past & Approach. I use to consider QM when the HH and LL just break a little the previous H and L. As I understand, and as I said, I can't talk too loudly about my QM knowledge, what a bullish QM does is: 1) to cheat the sellers with the LL, that inmediatly goes up, getting fuel for the way up. 2) to cheat the buyers with the HH, that inmediatly goes down, cleaning the supply zone of orders, and letting free way for the up movement. But the HH also tell us that the downtrend probably has finish https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=175 25/34 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 8 - RTM Community 3) Then price go back to the next demand zone, from where goes up, completing the QM. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Oedipus qm hw. #195 okami Offline Associate Trader Posts: 359 Thank you received: 352 Of course, I was trying to point out many things. What I meant was that I would not qualify what you're showing as a QM, because the Higher High has gone too far away, on a unproportioned way respect of the rest of the QM. That was my impression when I show also this other chart you shared. The LL is https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=175 27/34 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 8 - RTM Community unproportioned to the rest of the QM. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT But this one I would consider a proper QM. It is proportioned. It makes a HH, but then a LL that shows the trend is changing. It has not a HH or LL that gets over a lot of previous H or L. In the chart we are discussing, although, there is what I would consider a proper QM, as I signal the yellow HH, that just gets over the previous H, showing bull intentions. Then price came back to demand, and then shoots up. So one of the interpretations we could do of a QM is that price is taking out orders on both sides with the HH and LL. Why? Because over the Highs and Lows there use to be clusters of orders. As breakout trading and SL over the Highs and Lows is one of the most extended ways of trading ("if resistance is broken, then buy, and put SL under the https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-quasimodo/31-the-quasimodo?start=175 28/34 7/27/2018 The Quasimodo - Page 8 - RTM Community last low"), there use to be a lot of orders. This order positions are well known, so when HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT price goes over a H or L they trigger a lot of orders. But what happen if price inmediately goes the other way? panic and SL triggering that add fuel to the movement. In this charts, a lot of sellers were trapped on the LL, that became buyers when their SL were triggered, adding fuel to the bull movement. At the same time the retail uninformed sellers were being the counterpart of the big money buyers, that need a lot of sellers to fulfill their orders. On this chart we could read that then price arrives to a Supply level, doing a HH. There were yet sell orders, so price came back to the next demand where the QM completed. When price did the HH it shows the bull strength, and consumed the few Sell orders that were left on the level. So the level was cleaned, and the sellers that were trapped on the LL that started triggering their SL, the way to the highs was ready, and as it happens, it shoots up. IF explains what I'm trying to say much better than me.
